summary: The Moon's ten-year mahadasha is described as a generally pleasant period: peace of mind, comfort, good food, gains of clothes, ornaments, land and cattle, marriage or children, and favour from those in authority. All sources make the outcome depend on the Moon's strength. A strong, waxing or well-placed Moon gives the full good results. A debilitated, waning, afflicted or 6th/8th/12th-house Moon brings loss of money, worry, trouble to the mother and friction with authorities.
themes: strength depends on the Moon's phase
common_outcomes: opulence, good fortune, gain of wealth, auspicious functions at home, high position, vehicles, clothes, children and cattle when the Moon is strong and well placed (BPHS 47.16-22)
tranquillity of mind, success in all business, good food, wife and children, ornaments, clothes, gems, cows and lands; honouring Brahmins (Phaladeepika 19.7)
money through sacred prayers, deities, Brahmins and royal favour; women, wealth and lands; flowers, clothes, ornaments and perfumes (Phaladeepika 19.19; Jataka Parijata 18.73)
misunderstandings with wicked people, some loss of money, wind-related illness (Phaladeepika 19.19)
loss of wealth when the Moon is debilitated or waning (BPHS 47.23-26)
rare_outcomes: extraordinary wealth and luxuries when the strong Moon is in the 2nd house (BPHS 47.16-22)
gain of a deposit or hidden treasure and acquisition of learning, with the Moon in the 2nd (BPHS 47.21-22, Sanskrit gloss)
digging tanks and building gardens or public works (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI, tr. P.S. Sastri, p. 144)
unexpected finding of treasure (Raman, Moon in Cancer)
death of the mother (Raman, Moon in Virgo)

by_area.personality: Calm and contented mind when the Moon is strong (Phaladeepika 19.7). With malefics: dullness, mental tension (BPHS 47.23-26); irritability (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI). Waning or descending Moon: mental worry and derangement (Raman).
by_area.career: High position in government, recognition from rulers, success in undertakings (BPHS 47.16-22); success in all business (Phaladeepika 19.7); taking charge of a new office (Raman, Moon in Pisces). Inimical relations with government when a waning Moon is in the 6th, 8th or 12th or with malefics (BPHS 47.23-26); trouble from employees (BPHS 47.23-26).
by_area.finance: Gain of wealth, vehicles, clothes, cattle and land (BPHS 47.16-22; Phaladeepika 19.7, 19.19); wealth that keeps increasing when the Moon is strong (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI). Loss of wealth if the Moon is debilitated, waning or with malefics (BPHS 47.23-26); want of food and loss of money if the Moon is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); poverty if anything checks the Moon's strength (Jataka Parijata 18.73).
by_area.health: Good health when the Moon is strong. Wind-related disease (Phaladeepika 19.19; Jataka Parijata 18.73); ill health and fevers when the Moon is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); bodily sluggishness with a weak Moon joined by malefics (BPHS 47.24, Sanskrit gloss).
by_area.relationships: Acquisition of a wife, children and the company of women (Phaladeepika 19.7, 19.19); births of children (BPHS 47.16-22). Troubles to the wife when the Moon is descending from exaltation (Raman).
by_area.family: Auspicious functions at home (BPHS 47.16-22); well-being of the mother when the Moon is strong (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI). Distress to the mother when the Moon is waning, weak or with malefics (BPHS 47.23-26). Quarrels with relatives when the Moon is weak (Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI); domestic happiness with the Moon in Sagittarius (Raman).
by_area.spirituality: Devotion to deities and Brahmins, sacred prayers and recitation (Phaladeepika 19.7, 19.19; Jataka Parijata 18.73); visits to holy places with the Moon in Libra or Capricorn and reciting religious texts with the Moon in Pisces (Raman).

strengtheners: Moon exalted (Taurus) or in its own sign (BPHS 47.16-22)
Moon in a kendra or in the 5th, 9th or 11th (BPHS 47.16-22)
Moon joined or aspected by benefics, or full (waxing) and strong (BPHS 47.17, Sanskrit gloss)
Moon associated with the lords of the 9th, 10th or 4th (BPHS 47.16-22)
Moon in the 2nd house, especially in exaltation or its own sign (BPHS 47.21-22)
Moon full in the middle ten days of the lunar month (Phaladeepika 19.8)
Moon owning the 8th house does not spoil the period: the Sun and the Moon give good results even as 8th lords (Phaladeepika 20.41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: waning Moon in the 6th, 8th or 12th, or with malefics (BPHS 47.25)
Moon in the last ten days of the lunar month: effects decline gradually (Phaladeepika 19.8)
anything that checks the Moon's strength (Jataka Parijata 18.73)
a natural benefic in debilitation, an enemy's sign or the 6th or 12th gives only untoward results (Phaladeepika 20.27, general rule)
kendra lordship spoils natural benefics; the Moon's blemish is ranked after Jupiter, Venus and Mercury (Phaladeepika 20.50-51)
lagna_or_context_notes: BPHS judges the period from the Moon's dignity, phase, house from the lagna, associations and the lords it joins. Phaladeepika 19.8 says everything in this period must be judged from the Moon's strength by phase: moderate in the first ten days of the lunar month, full in the middle ten, declining in the last ten. Functional role: Phaladeepika 20.41 (Parashara's view) exempts the Moon from the 8th-lord blemish, while 20.50-51 says a natural benefic owning a kendra turns less helpful, the Moon less so than Jupiter, Venus or Mercury. Raman gives separate results for the Moon in each sign, in the lagna, debilitated, in moolatrikona and when moving from exaltation towards debilitation.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.16-26, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 579-580
source_views.view: Throughout the period: opulence, good fortune, wealth, auspicious functions at home, a high position, vehicles, clothes, children and cattle, if the Moon is exalted, in its own sign, in a kendra, in the 11th, 9th or 5th, joined or aspected by benefics, fully powerful and associated with the 10th, 9th or 4th lord. Extraordinary wealth if such a Moon is in the 2nd. Debilitated or waning: loss of wealth. In the 3rd: happiness off and on. With malefics: dullness, mental tension, trouble from employees and the mother, loss of wealth. Waning in the 6th, 8th or 12th or with malefics: enmity with government, loss of wealth, distress to the mother. Strong in the 6th, 8th or 12th: troubles alternating with good spells.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.16-26, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 17 lists exaltation, own sign, a kendra, the 11th or a trine, benefic conjunction, fullness and strength. Verse 18 adds the 10th and 9th lords and the lord of vehicles (4th). Verse 19 reads the Moon 'in the house' (taken as the 4th): vehicles, audience with rulers, Lakshmi at home. Verses 21-22: in the 2nd, exalted or own: sons, cattle, treasure, learning. Verse 23: debilitated or waning, loss of wealth; strong in the 3rd, wealth and happiness come intermittently. Verse 26: a strong but badly placed Moon gives the mother's distress and mental anguish mixed with gains; shanti is advised.

19.7: tranquillity of mind, success in all undertakings, good food, wife, children, ornaments, clothes, gems, cows and lands, honouring Brahmins. 19.8: everything is to be stated after weighing the Moon's strength. It is moderate in the first ten days of the lunar month, full and very auspicious in the middle ten, and declining in the last ten. 19.19: money through prayers, gods, Brahmins and royal favour; women, wealth, lands, flowers, clothes, ornaments and perfumes; also disputes with the wicked, loss of money and wind disease.

General rules that bear on the Moon. 20.27: benefics in debilitation, an enemy's sign, the 6th or the 12th give only untoward results. 20.33: planets in prishtodaya signs give results at the end of their period, ubhayodaya in the middle, shirshodaya at the beginning. 20.41: the Sun or the Moon give good effects even as 8th lords. 20.50-51: kendra lordship makes Jupiter and Venus most harmful, then Mercury, then the Moon.

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.73, 18.83 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: 18.73: sacred prayers, scripture and Brahmins; charm over women; women, wealth and lands; flowers, clothes, ornaments and perfumes. If anything checks the Moon's strength, poverty and wind disease. 18.83: the house the Moon presides over gives results at the start of the period; the nature of that sign and the Moon's position show in the middle; the aspects on the Moon and the body part of that house show at the end.

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita ch. VI 'Results of the Major Periods of Planets' (tr. P.S. Sastri), p. 144; verse number not legible in the scan
source_views.view: A highly beneficial, powerful Moon gives the mother's well-being, digging of tanks, lands, gardens, a house, blessings of the twice-born, wealth, auspicious events and palanquins. A malefic Moon gives want of food, misery, loss of pleasure and money, ill health, lack of learning, irritability, being disliked, and malarial fevers.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 238-240
source_views.view: Results by sign: Aries, physical and mental happiness, contentment. Taurus, fame and great wealth. Gemini, education and property. Cancer, wealth, success in litigation, treasure, travel. Leo, education, unexpected gains. Virgo, death of the mother, enemies, restlessness. Libra, wealth, friends, pilgrimage, success. Scorpio, fear of rulers, loss of relatives, wealth, liberty and honour. Sagittarius, domestic happiness. Capricorn, lands, houses, new ventures, pilgrimage. Aquarius, loss of property, fear of authorities, family misunderstandings. Pisces, new office, religious texts, easy gains. In the lagna, charity and good friends. Descending from exaltation: losses, trouble to the wife, mental derangement, fear of rulers and poison. Debilitated: losses and worry. Moolatrikona: respect from rulers, money, land, happiness.

source_views.source: V.G. Rele, Directional Astrology of the Hindus, pp. 67-71
source_views.view: Gives no separate result for the Moon's major period as a whole. His general rules: a planet is in dignity when exalted, own, friendly, with benefics, with the 1st, 9th or 10th lord, or in a kendra, trikona or 11th from the lagna; a benefic owning a kendra is weakened. Planets in the 2nd or 7th cause illness even if not debilitated.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers ch. 6, pp. 202-203
source_views.view: General rule only: the major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. A benefic major period gives seeds of good results at its start rather than immediate fruit. The start of a period is the time for remedies: strengthen a weak benefic with its gem, propitiate a malefic with mantra or worship.

disagreements: BPHS and Uttara Kalamrita make the whole period good or bad by the Moon's strength and placement. Phaladeepika 19.19 and Jataka Parijata 18.73 give fixed mixed results: comforts together with some loss of money and wind disease. Santhanam reads BPHS 47 as one long list of favourable conditions; the Sanskrit gloss splits it and reads verse 19 as the Moon in the 4th, a placement Santhanam does not mention. In BPHS 47.23 Santhanam gives the Moon in the 3rd 'happiness off and on'; the gloss says a strong Moon there brings wealth and happiness intermittently. Raman's sign results (bad in Virgo and Aquarius, good in Libra and Capricorn) are not found in the BPHS or Phaladeepika chapters read. Phaladeepika 20.41 exempts the Moon from the 8th-lord blemish but 20.50-51 still counts its kendra lordship as a mild blemish.
phrasing_guidance: Describe this as a period whose tone follows the Moon's condition: comfort, home life and emotional steadiness when the Moon is strong; worry, money strain and concern for the mother when it is weak. Say waxing or waning plainly, as a matter of strength. Do not predict the mother's death or any illness as certain; frame health points as times to rest and look after the body.

phases: Jataka Parijata 18.83: at the start of the Moon's period come the results of the house the Moon rules over; in the middle, results from the nature of that sign and the Moon's own position; towards the end, results from the planets aspecting the Moon and to the part of the body that house governs. Phaladeepika 20.33 (general rule): a planet in a shirshodaya sign gives its results early in its period, in an ubhayodaya sign in the middle, and in a prishtodaya sign at the end. Frawley (pp. 202-203, general): a benefic period gives seeds at its start and fruit later.
